items.stem: What is the most accurate description of what a current brain-computer interface does?

options.text: It detects patterns in brain signals and decodes them into a limited set of control commands
options.rationale: Correct: BCIs decode measurable signal patterns into constrained commands, not detailed thoughts.

options.text: It reads a person's full inner thoughts as sentences
options.rationale: No current BCI reads detailed thoughts; this is speculation/hype.

options.text: It writes arbitrary memories directly into the brain
options.rationale: Writing memories is not an established BCI capability.

options.text: It requires no signal processing of any kind
options.rationale: BCIs depend heavily on signal processing and decoding.

items.explanation: Correct: BCIs decode measurable signal patterns into constrained commands, not detailed thoughts.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO trade-offs correctly contrast invasive and non-invasive BCIs? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Invasive electrodes can offer higher signal fidelity
options.rationale: Correct: implanted electrodes typically capture higher-quality signals.

options.text: Non-invasive methods avoid surgical risk but often have noisier signals
options.rationale: Correct: non-invasive approaches trade signal quality for safety and convenience.

options.text: Non-invasive methods always outperform invasive ones in signal quality
options.rationale: Non-invasive signals are generally noisier, not superior.

options.text: Invasive methods carry no medical risk
options.rationale: Invasive methods carry surgical and long-term medical risks.

items.explanation: Correct: implanted electrodes typically capture higher-quality signals.

items.stem: Why is per-user calibration typically required for a BCI?

options.text: Brain signals vary between individuals and over time, so the decoder must be tuned to the user
options.rationale: Correct: inter-person and session variability require calibration for reliable decoding.

options.text: Because calibration charges the device battery
options.rationale: Calibration tunes the decoder; it is not a charging step.

options.text: Because one universal decoder already works perfectly for everyone
options.rationale: Signals differ across people, so no universal decoder suffices.

options.text: Because calibration encrypts the neural data
options.rationale: Calibration is about decoding accuracy, not encryption.

items.explanation: Correct: inter-person and session variability require calibration for reliable decoding.
